hero.title: Winter Courses in Sweden for Indian Students
paras: **Winter Courses in Sweden** offer international students an opportunity to experience Nordic winter life while studying subjects such as sustainability, business, environmental science, Swedish culture and technology. These short-term programmes may include classroom learning, cultural activities, field visits and opportunities to connect with students from different countries.

highlights.title: World-Class Nordic Innovation
highlights.desc: Study in Sweden's globally ranked universities renowned for pioneering scientific breakthroughs, design thinking, and sustainable research.

highlights.title: English-Taught Degrees
highlights.desc: Over 1,000 bachelor's and master's degree programs delivered entirely in English with international accreditation.

highlights.title: Generous Post-Study Work

highlights.title: High Quality of Life
highlights.desc: Ranked among the top nations globally for safety, equality, environmental sustainability, and student well-being.

overview: For students considering winter study during **2026–2027**, several programmes may be worth exploring. Jönköping University's Youth Winter School is scheduled for **7–18 December 2026**, while Linköping University's winter programme for eligible exchange students runs from **30 November 2026 to 24 January 2027**.
Admission, availability and fees depend on each programme's requirements. Students should confirm the latest information with the respective university before applying.
Through **Edu Hawk worldwide** study abroad guidance, students can explore language-learning options and understand the eligibility, fees and application requirements.

universities.name: \. Jönköping University
universities.desc: ![][image1] Jönköping University's **Youth Winter School**, scheduled for **7–18 December 2026**, is designed for high-school students aged 16–18. The programme focuses on Swedish heritage, sustainability, innovation, English-language skills and cultural activities. It also includes a trip to Stockholm. Students should consult the university's official Winter School webpage or contact the organiser for current application arrangements, fees and availability.

universities.name: \. Linköping University
universities.desc: ![][image2] Linköping University's **Winter Programme** runs during the winter period, with the 2026–2027 programme scheduled from **30 November 2026 to 24 January 2027**. It includes short courses in subjects such as: * International Business * Development Economics * Environmental Monitoring * Digitalisation * Financial Markets The programme is open to eligible exchange students nominated by their home universities. Independent applicants should check the official programme conditions before considering an application.

universities.name: \. Luleå University of Technology
universities.desc: ![][image3] The **Arctic Winter School** explores subjects such as snow and ice, climate change, polar environments, innovation and cultural heritage. The Spring 2027 course is offered in English in Kiruna. However, the advertised application route is intended for eligible exchange students. Applicants should confirm the nomination requirements, course dates and participation arrangements with the university.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Winter Courses in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Winter Courses in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Winter Courses in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
